craft_notes: Sthāyin: ānanda as entry (praveśa — ingress, NOT feeling); vyabhicāri wonder at things disclosed as-they-are. Sanskrit-first: prabuddha (DAWNED-awakened — perfect: already risen); amṛta-pūrṇa (NECtar-FULL — pūrṇa modifies the LORD, kept attached); praviśāmi (I ENTER — first person enters, not feels). Rows: 1 (‘enter bliss’ closes — entry, the verse's whole doctrine, last), 8 (vowel arc bright throughout: dawn-rays-reveal → brimming-full — ānanda does not fall, it fills; no dark close), 7 declined — no vocative; locative ‘In You’ carries address. Close: ‘I myself enter bliss’. Rupture: colon after ‘essence’ (disclosure turns to entry — seeing turns to entering). Rejected: ‘I feel bliss’ — killed: ingress ≠ feeling (C1 explicit); ‘full of nectar’ reordering — killed: pūrṇa belongs to the Lord; ‘true nature’ for ‘true essence’ — killed: tattva kept essence. Read aloud: TRUE a-WAK-en-ing HAS-dawned — its RAYS re-VEAL … IN-you — BRIMM-ing-FULL of su-PREME-nec-tar — i-my-SELF EN-ter BLISS.

lines: True awakening has dawned — its rays reveal each thing’s true essence:
In You — brimming full of supreme nectar — I myself enter bliss.
l4.sanskrit_cite: proditasatyavibodhamarīciprekṣitaviśvapadārthasatattvaḥ bhāvaparāmṛtanirbharapūrṇe tvayi aham ātmani nirvṛtim emi

reads_against.argmap: What does true awakening disclose, and what is bliss? → Awakening discloses things as they are; bliss is entry into the Lord's fullness — ingress, not feeling.
c1_essence: True awakening discloses things as they are: its rays reveal the true essence of world-objects.
In You, being-full, I the self enter bliss — ingress, not feeling.
Awakening discloses; entry is bliss; pūrṇa (full/complete) is the Lord's nature.
